target: cross-cutting (all three models + measurement + estimator + metric)

proposals.name: P1. A limits-to-arbitrage price wedge: a slow-moving, idiosyncratic demand shock whose amplitude is a firm-specific arbitrage-cost multiplier
proposals.one_line: Multiply every model's observed price by exp(-kappa_i * v_it) with v_i an independent AR(1) and kappa_i a nonlinear (size, idio-vol) arbitrage-cost loading; this is the only change that creates the unspanned premium the three models structurally lack, and it costs three lines inside each sdf_compute.
proposals.economic_story: All three models are frictionless rational-expectations economies in which mu_t is BY CONSTRUCTION minus the conditional covariance of returns with the representative agent's SDF. That is exactly DKKM's 'APT' calibration, in which complexity is provably worthless. Real cross-sections are AIPT: the marginal investor differs across stocks, noise-trader/index/flow demand moves prices away from the arbitrageur's valuation, and the deviation survives in proportion to arbitrage cost (Shleifer-Vishny 1997; Pontiff 2006; Stambaugh-Yu-Yuan 2015; DeLong-Shleifer-Summers-Waldmann 1990 noise-trader risk). Formalization that avoids the word 'mispricing': a two-agent economy in which the marginal holder of stock i is a constrained/segmented investor with a mean-reverting demand shock v_it, and the arbitrageur -- whose conditional frontier is what evaluate_sdfs scores against -- faces a position limit. The observed price is P^obs = P^model * exp(-kappa_i v_it). The wedge is stationary, mean-zero, and carries no aggregate risk, so it changes nothing about the model's internal equilibrium or its solution files; it is a pricing/holding-cost layer, not a change to the firm's problem. This is the AIPT world that DKKM show is the necessary and sufficient environment for the virtue of complexity.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: Write R^obs_{i,t+1} = R_{i,t+1} * exp(q_it - q_{i,t+1}) with q_it = kappa_it v_it. Then E_t[R^obs_i] = E_t[R_i]*exp(q_it - kappa_{i,t+1} rho v_it + 0.5 kappa_{i,t+1}^2 sigma_v^2), so the conditional excess return gains alpha_i = (1-rho) q_it + O(kappa^2), and the conditional variance gains an idiosyncratic term kappa_i^2 sigma_v^2 that is independent of every aggregate shock. Two consequences. (i) UNSPANNED PREMIUM: alpha is orthogonal to the 1-2 factor loadings, so it contributes alpha' D^{-1} alpha ~ N * E[alpha^2/d] to SR*^2, a quantity that GROWS with N. This is the AIPT near-arbitrage; without it, span2.py shows every basis (equal-weight included) attains SR* to within 0.2% at N=1000, and no estimator change can matter. (ii) NONLINEAR TRUE WEIGHT: the true MVE weight becomes w*_i is proportional to alpha_i/d_i = (1-rho) kappa_i v_it / (d_fund,i + kappa_i^2 sigma_v^2). This is a product-over-sum: a product kappa_i x v_it in the numerator and a kappa_i^2 in the denominator, with kappa_i = exp(-phi*size_i + psi*log d_i) an exponential function of the characteristics. If additionally kappa_p90 * sigma_v >= sigma_idio,fund, w* is NON-MONOTONE (hump-shaped) in kappa with peak at kappa* = sigma_idio,fund/sigma_v: the least-arbitrageable firms carry the most mispricing but also the most noise-trader risk, so the optimal position rises then falls. A Fourier basis with adequate bandwidth approximates any smooth function of the chars and therefore reaches this; a linear span and a monotone tercile sort cannot. Note also that the chars reveal q ENDOGENOUSLY -- log bm^obs = log bm_fund + q, size^obs = size_fund - q, and mom picks up the q innovations -- so nothing about the signal is hand-planted into the panel.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: FM's portfolios are the columns of X(X'X)^{-1}, i.e. its span is EXACTLY {weights linear in the characteristics}, re-fit monthly. w*_i = (1-rho) kappa(x_i) v(x_i) / (d_f(x_i) + kappa(x_i)^2 sigma_v^2) is a product of two char functions divided by a sum containing the square of one of them; it is not in the linear span for any monthly coefficient vector, and it is not made linear by monthly re-estimation because the nonlinearity is CROSS-SECTIONAL, not temporal. FF's 2x3 sorts do contain exactly one interaction, size x char, at 2x3 step-function resolution -- so FF gets a coarse two-bin approximation of the kappa(size) modulation of one signal, but (a) it cannot form the 1/(d_f + kappa^2 sigma_v^2) division at all, (b) it cannot form a triple interaction (size x idio-vol x signal), and (c) a tercile long-short is by construction MONOTONE in the sort variable, so it is structurally incapable of representing the hump in kappa: it will short exactly the firms whose alpha is largest. Both benchmarks therefore leave the entire ratio and the entire non-monotonicity on the table, which is measurable as the population span gap SR_rff/SR_lin.
proposals.exact_change: NEW FILE utils_wedge/wedge.py with two functions. (1) simulate_wedge(N, T, rng) -> (q, kappa) : draw log kappa_i ~ Normal(log kappa_med, s_k^2) as a PERMANENT firm attribute, or set kappa_{i,t+1} = kappa_med * (mve_it/median_t)^{-phi} * (sigma_idio,it/median_t)^{psi} which is PREDETERMINED at t and therefore keeps everything analytic; simulate v_{i,t+1} = rho v_it + sigma_v eps, eps ~ iid N(0,1) independent of every model shock; q_it = kappa_it v_it. (2) apply_wedge(ER_risky, eret, q_t, kappa_next, rho, v_t, sigma_v) implementing: m = exp(-kappa_next*rho*v_t + 0.5*kappa_next**2*sigma_v**2); a = exp(q_t)*m; ER_obs = a[:,None]*ER_risky*a[None,:]; np.fill_diagonal(ER_obs, np.diag(ER_obs)*np.exp(kappa_next**2*sigma_v**2)); eret_obs = a*(1+eret) - 1.  CALL SITES, three lines each: utils_bgn/sdf_compute_bgn.py after line 285 (ER[1:,1:] /= np.outer(P[t+1],P[t+1])) and before line 288, replacing eret[t+1,:] at lines 288-290, 320, 323, 326 with eret_obs; utils_kp14/sdf_compute_kp14.py after line 229 (the term_diag assignment) and before line 257, replacing eret[t,:] at 257-259, 291; utils_gs21/sdf_compute_gs21.py after line 197 and before line 199, replacing eret[t,:] at 199-201, 221-223, 229. PANEL SIDE: utils_bgn/panel_functions_bgn.py line 212 mve = P[:-1] becomes P[:-1]*exp(-q[:-1]) and line 217 ret becomes (1+ret)*exp(q[:-1]-q[1:]) - 1, done BEFORE bm/mom/agr are constructed at lines 247-260 so the chars inherit the contamination; the same two-line edit in utils_kp14/panel_functions_kp14.py (price/rets) and utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py (P_ex/ret, line 131 region). CONFIG: add WEDGE_RHO, WEDGE_SD_V, WEDGE_KAPPA_MED, WEDGE_SD_LOG_KAPPA, WEDGE_PHI, WEDGE_PSI to config.py near line 200. NOTHING in kp14_fd.py, integ_kp14.py or the GS21 MATLAB solfiles changes -- the wedge is applied to the observed price, not to the firm's optimization.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: Four numbers. (1) PERSISTENCE. Anomaly mispricing half-lives in the correction literature are 1-3 years; take 18 months, so rho = 0.5^(1/18) = 0.9622, 1-rho = 0.0378. Normalize the stationary sd of v to 1, hence sigma_v = sqrt(1-rho^2) = 0.2724. (2) MEDIAN AMPLITUDE kappa_med, pinned by the TARGET maximum Sharpe rather than by the misvaluation literature. alpha_i = (1-rho) kappa_i v_it has cross-sectional sd (1-rho)*kappa_i, and SR_alpha^2 = sum_i alpha_i^2/d_i ~ N*(1-rho)^2*E[kappa^2/d]. With N=1000, sigma_idio = 10%/month (the P5 target), and a dispersion correction M ~ 1.5 for s_k = 0.8: kappa_med = SR_alpha_target * sigma_idio / (sqrt(N)*(1-rho)*M) = 0.6*0.10/(31.62*0.0378*1.5) = 0.033. So a 3.3% log-price wedge for the median firm delivers SR_alpha = 0.6/month = 2.1 annualized on top of the factor Sharpe. Target justification: DKKM's five-characteristic real-data result is FF6 = 0.74 annual -> complex 1.93-2.50 annual, i.e. 2.6-3.4x; with SR_factor = 0.21/month (= FF6's 0.74 annual, and close to BGN's current FF Sharpe of 0.2423) a total SR* = sqrt(0.21^2+0.6^2) = 0.636/month = 2.20 annual reproduces that ratio exactly. Note the tension worth disclosing: 3.3% is CONSERVATIVE relative to Rhodes-Kropf-Robinson-Viswanathan, whose firm-specific misvaluation component has sd ~0.40 in logs -- the binding constraint here is the reported SR*, not realism. (3) DISPERSION s_k = sd(log kappa). Set from the arbitrage-cost cross-section: DKKM report SDF Sharpe 3.7 full-sample versus ~1.6 in mega/large caps, a 2.3x concentration in small caps, and illiquidity/arbitrage-cost proxies span 1-2 orders of magnitude. s_k = 1.0 gives a p10-p90 kappa ratio of exp(2.563*1.0) = 13x. HUMP CONDITION (optional but valuable): the non-monotonicity of w* in kappa requires kappa_p90 >= sigma_idio,fund/sigma_v = 0.10/0.2724 = 0.367. With kappa_med = 0.033 that needs s_k = log(0.367/0.033)/1.282 = 1.88. So there is an explicit trade-off: s_k = 1.0 buys the product/ratio nonlinearity only; s_k ~ 1.9 additionally buys the hump but raises SR* (E[kappa^2/d] is dominated by the right tail). Recommendation: run s_k in {0.8, 1.3, 1.9} and report SR* for each; pick the largest s_k for which SR* stays below ~2.5 annualized. (4) CHAR LOADINGS phi, psi. Self-calibrating so the same rule works in all three models despite their different char dispersions: phi = log(3)/(2.563*sd(log mve_model)) so that the p10-p90 size range spans a 3x kappa ratio (matching DKKM's 2.3x mega-vs-all Sharpe ratio), and psi = log(2)/(2.563*sd(log d_model)) so the idio-vol range spans 2x. Numerically for BGN with sd(log mve) ~ 0.6, phi = 1.099/1.538 = 0.71; for GS21 with sd(log mve) = 0.285, phi = 1.50.
proposals.predicted_effect: Using span2.py's measured population ceilings for the 'nonlinear alpha + heteroskedastic d' cell as the upper bound and the 'linear alpha + het d' cell as the lower: DKKM/FM population span ratio moves from 0.99-1.00 today to 1.9-6.4, and the est3.py Monte Carlo with T=360 estimation noise turns that into a realized ratio of 2-11x with a MONOTONICALLY RISING Sharpe-vs-nfeatures curve (currently flat at +2.5%). Concretely at the SR_alpha = 0.6/month calibration: max_sr rises from 0.2985 to ~0.64/month for BGN (2.2 annualized, a credible number and a big improvement on KP14's current artifactual 10/month); FF and FM Sharpes rise only slightly, because most of the new alpha is outside their span -- expect FF 0.24 -> 0.28, FM 0.236 -> 0.30; DKKM at 3600-36000 features with a recentered alpha rises to 0.55-0.75, i.e. a DKKM/FF ratio of 2-2.7x. HJD (once made scale-free per P4) should go from FF ~0.92x DKKM today to DKKM ~0.45-0.55x FF, matching DKKM's real-data 0.22 vs 0.45-0.9. Sharpe/SR* (the Sigma-cosine, per P4) should read roughly FF 0.42, FM 0.46, DKKM 0.90.
risks: REFEREE RISK, the big one: 'you added mispricing by hand, of course a flexible estimator finds it.' Mitigations: (i) frame as segmented markets / heterogeneous marginal investors, not irrationality -- the arbitrageur's frontier is still what is scored; (ii) point out this is literally DKKM's own AIPT assumption, and that under APT they PROVE complexity strictly reduces the Sharpe ratio, so an APT model cannot be the test bed; (iii) do not place the nonlinearity by hand -- kappa is a function of size and idio vol only, and the hump and the ratio EMERGE from Sigma^{-1}mu, they are not written down.

The wedge contaminates the characteristics, which is a feature (it makes q discoverable) but also means bm, size and mom are no longer clean functions of fundamentals; check that the fundamental value-premium and size-premium survive.

If kappa is made time-varying it must be PREDETERMINED at t (a function of date-t observables) or the analytic ER transform breaks. Using kappa_{i,t+1} = g(x_it) is fine; using kappa_{i,t+1} = g(x_{i,t+1}) is not.

exp(q) with a fat-tailed kappa can create extreme prices; winsorize q at, say, +/- 3 stationary sd, and re-check the conditioning of ER (KP14 already has a zero-book singularity and GS21 has an arbitrary P_ex floor at panel_functions_gs21.py:131).

In KP14 this cannot be evaluated at all until the corrupt integ_results.npz (integ_kp14.py:43, scipy.quad returning exact zeros over the eps range where 98% of firm-months live) and the stale G_func.csv are fixed; the KP14 'truth' is currently a numerical artifact.
proposals.implementation_cost: Negligible in the O(N^2) core: apply_wedge is a rank-preserving symmetric rescale ER -> diag(a) ER diag(a) plus a diagonal multiply, i.e. O(N^2) elementwise on a matrix that is already being formed, and O(N) for the a and m vectors. No new quadrature, no new state to integrate over (v's innovation is Gaussian and independent, so its contribution is a closed-form lognormal moment). No re-solve of kp14_fd.py and no new GS21 MATLAB solfiles. The panel side adds one (T,N) array. Total new code ~80 lines plus ~6 call-site edits.

proposals.name: P2. Estimator geometry repair: bandwidth, the second rank-standardization, NMAT, the alpha grid, and c = P/T -- all derived, none tuned
proposals.one_line: Five config/one-line edits that turn the RFF map from an effectively 17-dimensional near-cubic basis into a genuinely high-dimensional one, and recentre the ridge grid on the region where the virtue of complexity lives; worth ~0 on the current models but a strict precondition for P1/P3/P4 to show up.
proposals.economic_story: Not economics -- estimator hygiene. But it is a precondition, and every item has a derivation rather than a tuning story, which is what disarms the 'you tuned the estimator to win' objection. Three of the five items are restorations of the published DKKM/root convention rather than deviations from it.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: (a) BANDWIDTH. sd(W x) = gamma*sqrt(L/12) because rank_standardize maps each char to variance 1/12. At L=5 and gamma <= 1.0 this is at most 0.645, measured 0.48-0.53; the closed-form R^2 of the linear projection of sin(u), u~N(0,s^2), is 2 s^2 e^{-s^2}/(1-e^{-2 s^2}) = 0.998/0.991/0.972 at gamma = 0.5/0.75/1.0. So sin is 97-99.8% linear and cos is a pure quadratic: the 3600-feature map has participation-ratio effective rank 16.5, 48.9% of its variance in the 6-dim linear span and 88.4% in the 56-dim cubic span. Nominal c = P/T = 10; EFFECTIVE c = 16.5/360 = 0.046, i.e. deep in the classical regime where the P/T asymptotics that generate the virtue of complexity never engage. (b) DOUBLE RANK-STANDARDIZATION. rank_standardize is invariant to monotone transformations and sin is monotone over the realized range for 76% of features, so corr(rank_std(sin(gamma g'x)), rank_std(g'x)) = 0.9997-0.9999 and GAMMA_GRID is a near-exact NO-OP; likewise rank_std(cos z) = rank_std(-|z|) exactly. Two features with the same direction but different |w| are literally the same column, so the dictionary is indexed only by the direction of w on the sphere in R^L (a 4-dim index at L=5) with two fixed shapes -- and the Rahimi-Recht kernel identity is broken, so the induced RKHS is not the Gaussian RKHS. It also forces every column to the same bounded uniform marginal, so no feature can be large-amplitude on a small subset of firms, which is exactly the shape needed to represent a ratio b(x)/d(x) with a small denominator. (c) NMAT. Averaging M independent random-feature ridge fits of the SAME target on the SAME 360 months converges to KERNEL ridge with the same explicit penalty; the draw-specific high-frequency components eta_m cancel at rate 1/M, so the ensemble is strictly smoother than any single draw and the Sharpe-vs-nfeatures curve mechanically flattens. (d) ALPHA GRID. Effective df = sum lambda_j/(lambda_j + 360*P*alpha) is P-invariant; the BGN/KP14 grid gives df = [360, 63, 22, 9.5, 6.2, 1.15], with NO point anywhere in df in (63, 360) -- precisely the mildly-overparameterized region past the interpolation threshold where the virtue of complexity peaks. Four of six points sit at df <= 22. (e) COMPLEXITY RANGE. c tops out at 10 while DKKM's headline and their five-char result both use c = 1000.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Not applicable in the usual sense -- this proposal does not add anything for FF/FM to fail at; it removes the reason DKKM cannot reach what is already there. State it honestly: on the CURRENT three models the impact of this bundle is approximately zero, because the population span headroom is 0.7pp of Sharpe in BGN and 3% in GS21. Its value is entirely conditional on P1/P3/P4. The one thing it does independently is remove three referee attacks: 'your RFF basis was a quadratic', 'your alpha grid skipped the interesting region', and 'you gave DKKM oracle alpha selection and FF/FM none'.
proposals.exact_change: (a) config.py line 211: GAMMA_GRID = np.arange(0.5, 1.1, 0.1) becomes a per-model dict GAMMA_GRID_BY_MODEL[m] = np.arange(0.5,1.1,0.1)*np.sqrt(130/len(MODEL_CHARS[m])), read in utils/generate_dkkm_factors.py line 116. (b) utils_factors/dkkm_functions.py line 110: replace `return rank_standardize(features)` with a per-column z-score, `mu = features.mean(0); sd = features.std(0); sd[sd==0]=1.0; return np.ascontiguousarray((features-mu)/sd)`. DO NOT simply delete the second standardization: the audit measured that removing it makes things WORSE (linear-span share rises 48.9% -> 86.4%, effective rank falls 14.4 -> 5.1) because it is silently equalizing the sin and cos amplitudes, which differ 3.1x (sd(sin u)=0.415 vs sd(cos u)=0.135 at s=0.46). Z-scoring keeps the amplitude equalization AND restores gamma-dependence. (c) config.py line 178: NMAT = 5 -> 1 (the root codebase comment on line 177 already says nmat = 1); report the 5 draws as replications in create_slides_tables.py rather than averaging them in utils/estimate_sdf_dkkm.py lines 134-169. (d) config.py lines 190-193: replace ALPHA_LST / ALPHA_LST_GS with a single scale-free grid. Reparameterize the penalty in utils_factors/dkkm_functions.py lines 162 and 176 from 360*z to 360*z*trace(X'X)/P so that z is a pure shrinkage fraction, then set ALPHA_LST = [0, 1e-6, 3e-6, 1e-5, 3e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1, 1]. This also eliminates the GS21 /100 hand-tuning at line 193. (e) config.py line 181: N_DKKM_FEATURES_LIST = [6, 36, 360, 3600, 36000] so c = P/T spans 0.017 to 100. (f) FAIRNESS: config.py line 187 ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0] -> the same z-grid, and utils_factors/fama_functions.py line 270 Ridge(alpha=360*alpha) -> the same scale-free penalty; and in bop-analyze-remote/create_slides_tables.py lines 81-97, apply find_best_alpha_for_model to FF/FM as well as DKKM so both sides get the same post-hoc selection.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: BANDWIDTH: the object to hold fixed across L is the Gaussian-kernel exponent gamma^2 E|x-x'|^2/2 = gamma^2 * L/12 (each rank-standardized char has variance 1/12, so E|x-x'|^2 = 2L/12). Real-data DKKM run L = 130 with gamma in [0.5,1.0], giving exponent 5.42*gamma^2 and sd(Wx) = 3.291*gamma. Matching at L=5 requires gamma_sim = gamma*sqrt(130/5) = 5.099*gamma, i.e. GAMMA_GRID = [2.55, 3.06, 3.57, 4.08, 4.59, 5.10]; at L=6 (GS21) the factor is sqrt(130/6) = 4.655, giving [2.33, 2.79, 3.26, 3.72, 4.19, 4.66]. Measured consequences of the L=5 rescale: mean sd(Wx) 0.459 -> 2.368, P(|Wx| > pi/2) 0.74% -> 48.4%, fraction of sin features monotone across the cross-section 76% -> 0.4%, linear-span share 48.9% -> 14.1%, cubic-span share 88.4% -> 52.4%, participation-ratio effective rank 14.4 -> 77.8, k90 20 -> 228. CAVEAT WITH TEETH: the GS21 agent tested this directly and widening HURT wherever the truth was near-linear (36 features: 0.879 -> 0.799 of max SR^2 at gamma x4.65; 0.879 -> 0.376 at gamma x10). So the rescale must be applied jointly with P1/P3, and the honest reporting is a 2x2 of {old, rescaled} gamma x {old, new} DGP. Note also that P3 (raising L to ~35) delivers sd(Wx) = 1.708*gamma with the ORIGINAL grid, so expanding the characteristic set is the referee-proof, non-tuned route to the same place. ALPHA GRID: required alpha for a target df at the current parameterization is df=180 -> 6.6e-5, df=100 -> 3.4e-4, df=50 -> 1.7e-3, df=20 -> 1.2e-2, df=10 -> 4.6e-2, df=5 -> 1.4e-1, df=1 -> 1.18; the proposed 11-point log grid hits df = [360, 283, 220, 180, 130, 100, 63, 30, 10, 3, 1]. COMPLEXITY: c = 36000/360 = 100, one decade short of DKKM's 1000 but two decades past the current 10.
proposals.predicted_effect: On the models AS THEY STAND: essentially nothing -- BGN's entire population nonlinearity headroom is 0.7pp of Sharpe and GS21's is 3%, so expect DKKM Sharpe to move by less than 0.01 and possibly DOWN under the wider bandwidth. Two things WILL change visibly and should be reported as bug fixes: the c=1 double-descent spike (BGN HJD 18.52, GS21 23.57 at P=360, alpha=0) disappears once the grid has points at df in (63,360); and the alpha=0 column stops realizing 1.4-13% of max Sharpe. Conditional on P1/P3 being in place, this bundle is what converts a population span ratio of 1.9-6.4 into a realized one -- est3.py shows RFF(3600) at 1.249 versus lin at 0.071 under nonlinear alpha + heteroskedastic d, and that number is unreachable with the current basis whose effective rank is 16.5. HJD and max_sr unaffected by construction (max_sr is a property of the DGP).
risks: 'You tuned the estimator to win.' Partially mitigated by derivation (the bandwidth rescale holds the kernel exponent fixed at DKKM's own real-data value; NMAT=1 restores the published convention; the alpha reparameterization is scale-free and removes the existing GS21 hand-tuning), but the referee will still ask. The decisive mitigation is to give FF/FM the identical ridge grid and the identical post-hoc alpha selection, and to show DKKM wins anyway.
Widening gamma can strictly HURT if the truth stays near-linear -- measured, not hypothetical. Do not apply it before P1/P3.

Z-scoring the features changes the factor-return scale by a factor of sqrt(12) = 3.46 (rank weights have sum of squares N/12, z-scored weights have N), so X'X is 12x larger; the alpha reparameterization must land in the same commit or every existing alpha number becomes uninterpretable.
P = 36000 memory: the per-month feature matrix is 1000 x 36000 float64 = 288 MB, times 16 workers = 4.6 GB. Use float32 and drop n_jobs to 8, or stream the sin/cos halves.
NMAT=1 raises the Monte-Carlo variance of every DKKM cell; report the 5 draws as a distribution so the referee sees the spread rather than a single lucky draw.
proposals.implementation_cost: Zero impact on sdf_compute -- none of this touches the O(N^2) per-month moment computation or the analytic second moment. Roughly 25 edited lines across config.py, dkkm_functions.py, fama_functions.py, estimate_sdf_dkkm.py and create_slides_tables.py. Runtime rises with P = 36000 (about 10x the current DKKM step) but falls with NMAT = 1 (5x), so net roughly 2x.

proposals.name: P3. Expand the econometrician's characteristic set from 5-6 to ~35 model-generated, individually weak, partly redundant signals -- given identically to FF, FM and DKKM
proposals.one_line: Build multi-horizon, lagged, peer-relative and volatility-based transforms of quantities the three models already produce, raising L from 5-6 to ~35, which raises the RFF effective rank from 16.5 to ~250 and makes the coded bandwidth genuinely nonlinear WITHOUT touching GAMMA_GRID.
proposals.economic_story: Real characteristic sets are not 5 clean state variables; they are dozens of overlapping, individually weak, differently-lagged accounting and return-based transforms of a smaller number of latent economic quantities, none of which pins down a state. DKKM's headline uses 130 such signals. Crucially, DKKM's own five-characteristic experiment (size, value, investment, profitability, momentum -- exactly this project's set) still gives FF6 0.74 -> complex 1.93-2.50 in real data, which PROVES the characteristic count is not the fundamental cause; but it is the mechanical cause of the estimator sitting at effective rank 16.5 instead of ~500. The proposal is therefore framed as fixing the estimator's operating regime by realistic means rather than by tuning a hyperparameter.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: L enters the estimator only through sd(W x) = gamma*sqrt(L/12) and through the dimension of the direction sphere. Measured participation-ratio effective rank of the exact rff() code path: L=5 -> 16.50, L=6 -> 20.71, L=10 -> 38.51, L=20 -> 98.25, L=50 -> 432.4, L=130 -> 773.5. Fitting eta_p = p^{-a} over P=3600, effective rank 16.5 corresponds to a = 1.22, which sits between DKKM's APT calibration (a=2.0, EffRank ~2.5, complexity harmful) and their AIPT calibration (a=0.5, EffRank ~500, complexity valuable). L = 35 interpolates to EffRank ~200-260, which lands in the AIPT regime, and sd(W x) = gamma*sqrt(35/12) = 1.708*gamma, so with the ORIGINAL GAMMA_GRID the index sd already spans 0.85-1.71 and sin is materially nonlinear -- P3 delivers most of P2(a) as a by-product, with no hyperparameter touched. Second mechanism, independent of dimension counting: with 35 partly-redundant noisy proxies of the same 2-3 latent states, the efficient use of the information is a shrinkage-weighted AGGREGATION across many weak signals, which is exactly what ridge-over-a-rich-basis does and exactly what a 7-parameter OLS cannot do -- DKKM's 'limits to learning' channel. This is the one channel in the DKKM theory that does NOT require an unspanned premium, though on its own it is worth far less than P1.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Careful here, because at L=35 the honest answer is partially negative and must be stated: FM with 35 regressors spans every LINEAR combination of the 35 chars, and 35 parameters on 360 months is still estimable (2K/T = 19% squared-Sharpe loss, no longer negligible but not fatal). So the pure dimension-counting channel gives FM a real estimation-noise handicap that DKKM's shrinkage avoids -- that is a genuine but MODEST DKKM edge (the DKKM/KMZ variance channel), on the order of the 19% versus DKKM's ridge-optimal loss. The LARGE gap still has to come from P1's nonlinearity. What FF cannot do at L=35 is more decisive: 35 separate 2x3 double sorts produce 35 highly collinear long-short factors whose OLS tangency at T=360 is badly conditioned, which is why real-data FF-style benchmarks top out at 0.74-1.2 annual. Bottom line, stated honestly: P3 is an enabling and realism change, not by itself a source of a 3-5x gap.
proposals.exact_change: NEW FILE utils_factors/char_library.py with a single function expand_chars(panel) that operates on the assembled panel AFTER each model's create_panel, using only columns the models already produce (mve, book, op_cash_flow, xret, and for GS21 book_lev). Roughly 35 columns: (i) 5 multi-horizon momentum/reversal -- ret_{t-1}, cumret(2,6), cumret(7,12), cumret(13,36), cumret(37,60), built with the same groupby/shift idiom already at utils_bgn/panel_functions_bgn.py lines 248-253; (ii) 4 multi-horizon asset growth -- 1m, 12m, 36m, 60m log book change, generalizing line 255; (iii) 5 profitability -- roe_{t-1}, 12m mean roe, 36m mean roe, delta roe, sd of roe over 36m; (iv) 4 valuation anchors -- book/mve, 5yr-average-book/mve, cumulative-cashflow/mve, 5yr-average-cashflow/mve; (v) 5 risk -- 12m and 60m realized return sd, 12m realized market beta, 60m beta, 36m return skewness; (vi) 3 scale -- log mve, log book, 12m change in log mve; (vii) 4 lags -- 6m and 12m lags of size and bm; (viii) 5 peer-relative -- each of size, bm, roe, mom, vol minus the mean of the firm's 'industry', where industry is a fixed random partition into 10 groups correlated with the model's own permanent firm type (beta_j in BGN, lambda_f in KP14, initial k in GS21); (ix) 2 age/staleness -- months since firm entry, months since the last accounting update (see P6). CONFIG: config.py lines 219-224 CHARS_DEFAULT / CHARS_GS21 -> the expanded list; config.py lines 229-235 CHAR_TO_FACTOR must be extended so utils_factors/fama_functions.py lines 63-65 and 170-172 can name 35 factors. FF: fama_functions.fama_french lines 83-104 already loops over all non-size chars, so it scales automatically. FM: lines 159-165 scale automatically, but see the fairness note below. GUARD: the FF tercile logic at lines 86-88 degenerates when a char has >30% ties (this already breaks agr, which is 91% zeros in BGN and 98.8% zeros in GS21, giving q30 = q70 = 0 and an empty medium bucket) -- add a tie-aware split.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: L = 35 is chosen so that effective rank lands in DKKM's AIPT regime while keeping FM estimable. From the measured EffRank(L) grid, a local power fit gives EffRank ~ 16.5*(L/5)^1.42 over 5 <= L <= 50, so L=35 -> 16.5*7^1.42 = 262 (the fit overshoots at L=130, so read this as 200-260). DKKM's AIPT calibration has EffRank ~500 at P=360,000. FM feasibility: with K = L+2 = 37 factors and T = 360, the plug-in tangency loses about 2K/T = 20.6% of squared Sharpe, i.e. about 11% of Sharpe -- material but honest, and it is exactly the handicap DKKM's shrinkage is supposed to avoid; going to L = 60 would push FM to 34% squared-Sharpe loss and would look like sabotage. Bandwidth by-product: sd(W x) = gamma*sqrt(35/12) = 1.708*gamma, so the coded grid [0.5,1.0] gives index sd 0.85-1.71 and the closed-form R^2 of the linear projection of sin drops from 0.972 to 2*1.708^2*exp(-1.708^2)/(1-exp(-2*1.708^2)) = 0.32 at gamma=1.0 -- genuinely nonlinear with the ORIGINAL grid. FAIRNESS ANSWER (task item d): YES, FF and FM must be given exactly the same 35 characteristics and exactly the same macro conditioning; otherwise the paper measures an information advantage, not a complexity advantage, and a referee will say so immediately. Two specific fairness repairs required in the same commit: (1) DELETE the BGN-only rf_stand input to the RFF at utils_factors/dkkm_functions.py lines 95-96 -- FF/FM never see the interest rate (fama_functions._compute_monthly_fama line 200 passes only data[chars]), so it is an unearned conditioning variable for DKKM; it is also measurably worthless (65.6% of sin features are literally unchanged when rf_stand flips from -0.5 to +0.5, and span with the rf column is 89.9% of max versus 90.1% without). If macro conditioning is wanted, put it in the panel as cross-sectionally varying char-x-macro interaction columns available to all three methods -- a date-level variable has zero cross-sectional variation and therefore cannot enter any cross-sectional portfolio weight for anyone. (2) TURN ON the commented-out FM standardization at fama_functions.py lines 152-156. Currently FM regresses on RAW chars, mixing log-size of order 5 with bm of order 1, so pinvh's default rcond can truncate directions; with 35 raw chars of wildly different scales this becomes a real handicap and the DKKM win would be attributable to it. Note the mirror-image asymmetry that must be disclosed either way: DKKM rank-standardizes its inputs and FM does not, so any monotone re-labeling of a characteristic changes FM's span and leaves DKKM's untouched -- rank-standardizing both sides is the only defensible resolution.
proposals.predicted_effect: RFF effective rank 16.5 -> ~250; effective c = EffRank/T from 0.046 to 0.7, i.e. the P/T asymptotics finally engage. On the CURRENT DGPs: DKKM Sharpe roughly flat or slightly up (there is still nothing nonlinear to find), FM Sharpe DOWN by roughly 10% from the 37-parameter estimation cost, FF Sharpe down more from 35 collinear sorted factors -- so this alone would produce a spurious-looking DKKM/FM ratio of maybe 1.2-1.3x that is pure estimation efficiency, not span, and should be labelled as such. Combined with P1, this is what converts the population span ratio into a realized one and produces a RISING Sharpe-vs-nfeatures curve. max_sr unchanged (chars are measurement, not DGP). HJD improves for DKKM in proportion to Sharpe.
risks: The gain from L alone is an estimation-efficiency gain, not a span gain, and a referee who understands DKKM Theorem 3 will ask which one is driving the result. Report the population span ceiling (diagnostic D2: mean_t SR_rff/SR_lin using the true rp and cond_var) alongside the realized Sharpes so the two channels are separated.

Handicapping FM with 37 parameters can be read as sabotage. Pre-empt it by also reporting a ridge-regularized FM at the same z-grid -- if DKKM still wins against a properly shrunk 37-char linear model, the result is about nonlinearity.

Several of the derived chars will be degenerate in these models the way agr already is (91% ties in BGN, 98.8% in GS21). Rank-standardize's argsort tie-breaking turns a 91%-tied column into a persistent (0.92 autocorrelation) pseudo-random characteristic that enters every one of the 3600 features MULTIPLICATIVELY, raising the PCs needed for 99% of feature variance from 59 to 95. Screen every new char for tie fraction and drop or jitter anything above ~20%.

Panel memory: 35 columns x 1000 firms x 920 months is still small, but the 60-month rolling transforms require the burn-in to be extended from 200 to at least 260 months so the first eval month has a full history.
proposals.implementation_cost: None on sdf_compute -- characteristics are panel columns and never enter the conditional-moment computation. About 150 lines in char_library.py plus config and CHAR_TO_FACTOR edits. DKKM feature generation cost is unchanged (W is (P/2, L), so L only affects the trivial W @ X.T). FF factor generation cost scales linearly in L.

proposals.name: P4. Recalibrate the idiosyncratic-risk block in all three models: raise its level, raise its cross-sectional dispersion, and make that dispersion a NONLINEAR function of characteristics
proposals.one_line: Undo the three 10x idiosyncratic-volatility cuts (BGN's '0.1 factor', KP14's SIGMA_EPS/SIGMA_U, GS21's SIGMA_Z) to hit real-data targets of ~10%/month idio vol, average pairwise correlation ~0.17, and sd(log idio variance) ~1.1; this is worth almost nothing alone but is a large MULTIPLIER on P1.
proposals.economic_story: All three models were tuned down to a degree that has no real-data counterpart. Real US equities: average pairwise monthly return correlation 0.15-0.20, equal-weighted idiosyncratic monthly volatility ~10-13%, and a cross-sectional sd of log idiosyncratic variance of roughly 1.0-1.3 with a p10-p90 idio-vol ratio of 3-4x. Current: BGN idio 3.90%/month with pairwise correlation 0.565 and sd(log d) = 0.263; KP14 idio 4.69%/month with pairwise 0.391 and sd(log d) = 0.664 (and, after the 10x cut, 97.8% of that idiosyncratic variance is pure Poisson project-count lumpiness rather than productivity risk, which is what mechanically produces idio var ~ 1/size and hence the anti-size artifact behind KP14's negative Sharpes); GS21 idio 2.0-2.4%/month with pairwise correlation 0.95 and an idio/systematic ratio of 0.17 against a real-data value of about 2.2, i.e. off by 13x. Restoring these is not a modelling innovation, it is undoing three commits.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: Two distinct channels, both multiplicative on P1 rather than standalone. (i) THE D^{-1} TILT AS A MULTIPLIER. Under exact factor pricing the inverse-variance tilt is worth 1/(2 sigma_f^2 beta'D^{-1}beta), measured at 1.81% of SR* at N=100, 0.186% at N=1000, 0.019% at N=10000 -- it is worth essentially nothing on its own, EVEN with a 20x spread in d, because idiosyncratic risk is diversifiable. But in the presence of an unspanned alpha it is a large multiplier: span2.py measures the RFF/linear population ceiling ratio rising from 1.00 to 1.91 when heteroskedastic d is added to a LINEAR alpha (and the linear span's share of SR* collapsing from 1.00 to 0.31), and from 2.88 to 6.37 when added to a nonlinear alpha. The reason is structural: w* = alpha/d is a RATIO, so dispersion in the denominator is what converts a linear numerator into a nonlinear weight function. (ii) SIGNAL-TO-NOISE. Raising idio vol makes estimation genuinely hard, which is DKKM's 'limits to learning' precondition (C5). Currently FF/FM at K=7, T=360 lose only 2K/T = 3.9% of squared Sharpe, i.e. they sit at their population optimum with nothing for shrinkage to buy back. It also fixes two embarrassments in the tables: KP14's max_sr of 10/month (34.7 annualized against the model's own correct bound of 0.774 annualized) and GS21's max_sr of 0.44/month, 89-97% of which comes from diversifying 3.5-4.3 basis points of per-firm alpha across 500 nearly-identical firms with 2% idio vol -- a synthetic near-arbitrage with no real-data counterpart.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: FM's span is weights linear in x; the object it must reach is alpha(x)/d(x). Even when alpha and d are each exactly linear in x, the ratio is not, and the approximation error grows with the dispersion of d -- which is precisely the parameter this proposal raises. FF is worse: a 2x3 value-weighted double sort produces weights proportional to mve within a bucket, i.e. it weights firms by SIZE, whereas the efficient weight is proportional to 1/d; when d is strongly char-linked these two are close to orthogonal (KP14 is the extreme case, where idio var ~ 1/nlive ~ 1/size makes the true weight proportional to +size while every empirical tangency portfolio loads on the size premium, -size, giving a negative Sigma-cosine and hence the negative Sharpes with no sign bug anywhere). The one honest caveat: if d is a MONOTONE function of a single characteristic, FF's tercile sorts on that characteristic get a crude approximation of the tilt. So the dispersion should be driven by an interaction (size and a second variable), not by size alone.
proposals.exact_change: BGN: utils_bgn/panel_functions_bgn.py line 54, remove the '0.1*' from `high = np.abs(beta[:-1,:])/sigma_z + 0.1*0.3*np.abs(Cbar)`. This is a single inline edit flagged in the code by its own comment '# added a factor of 0.1'. KP14: config.py lines 248 and 250, KP14_SIGMA_EPS = 0.1*0.2 -> 0.2 and KP14_SIGMA_U = 0.1*1.5 -> 1.5. GS21: config.py line 289, GS21_SIGMA_Z = 0.1*0.16*sqrt(...) -> 0.5*0.16*sqrt(...). ADDITIONALLY, to make d char-linked NONLINEARLY rather than monotonically in size, ride on P1's wedge: the wedge contributes kappa_i^2 sigma_v^2 to d_i with kappa_i = kappa_med*(mve/median)^{-phi}*(sigma_idio/median)^{psi}, so total d_i = d_fund,i + kappa_med^2 sigma_v^2 (mve/med)^{-2phi}(sigma/med)^{2psi} -- a SUM of two power laws in two characteristics, which is not a power law and not linear. That is free once P1 is in.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: BGN: the current band is sigmaj ~ U[|beta|/sigma_z, |beta|/sigma_z + 0.1*0.3*|Cbar|] = U[|beta|/0.4, |beta|/0.4 + 0.111]. With E|beta| = 0.636 the lower bound averages 1.59, so the idiosyncratic width is 7% of the level and the implied SDF-cashflow correlation is forced to corr_zj = 0.958 with mean(1-corr_zj^2) = 0.0710 -- cash flows are 96% systematic. Removing the 0.1 makes the band 1.11 wide, raising mean(1-corr_zj^2) roughly 6x; idiosyncratic return variance scales with (1-corr_zj^2)*sigmaj^2, so idio vol goes from 3.90%/month to roughly 3.90*sqrt(6) = 9.6%/month, hitting the 10% target, and the idiosyncratic share of total variance goes from 46.9% to about 85%, giving an average pairwise correlation of about 0.15 against the real-data 0.15-0.20. sd(log d) should rise from 0.263 toward 0.8-1.0 because the width of the sigmaj band is what generates the dispersion. KP14: restoring SIGMA_EPS and SIGMA_U to 0.2 and 1.5 raises idiosyncratic variance 3.179x (measured: idio 2.481e-03 -> 7.887e-03), i.e. idio vol 4.69% -> 8.9%/month, and -- more important -- restores the CIR share of idiosyncratic variance from 2.2% to 69.2%, which BREAKS the idio var ~ 1/nlive ~ 1/size identity (currently corr(log idio var, log nlive) = -0.971) that is the direct cause of KP14's negative Sharpes. It also improves the conditioning of cond_var by 4.1x (condition number 680 -> 165). GS21: at 0.1x, idio vol is 2.0-2.4%/month against systematic 10.0-12.3%. Idio vol scales roughly linearly in sigma_z, so 0.5x gives about 10.5%/month and an idio/systematic ratio of 0.85, versus the current 0.17 and the real-data ~2.2; average pairwise correlation falls from 0.95 to about 0.58. Going all the way to the paper's 1.0x would give ~21%/month, overshooting, and would reopen two known traps -- so 0.5x is the recommendation. TARGETS RESTATED: idio vol ~10%/month; average pairwise conditional correlation 0.15-0.20; sd(log idio variance) ~1.0-1.3 (p10-p90 idio-vol ratio 3-4x).
proposals.predicted_effect: On its own: max_sr FALLS in all three models (BGN 0.2985 -> roughly 0.15-0.20/month as the diversification of the common premium weakens; KP14 falls sharply from its artifactual 10/month; GS21 from 0.44 toward 0.2), all methods' Sharpes fall roughly proportionally, and the DKKM/FF ratio moves by only a few percent. That is the honest standalone prediction and it is why this is ranked fourth. Combined with P1: this is the difference between span2.py's 'linear alpha, homogeneous d' cell (RFF/lin = 1.00) and its 'linear alpha, heteroskedastic d' cell (RFF/lin = 1.91), and between 'nonlinear alpha, homogeneous d' (2.88) and 'nonlinear alpha, heteroskedastic d' (6.37). Expect it to roughly DOUBLE whatever gap P1 produces. Also fixes the sign of KP14, which is currently uninterpretable.
risks: GS21 REQUIRES A MATLAB RE-SOLVE. The solfiles (P_up.csv, P_down.csv, z_cut_*.csv, dated 2026-06-10) were solved for the 0.1x sigma_z and their zgrid spans exactly +/-2.7247 stationary sd of that value; at 0.5x the grid covers only +/-0.54 sd and every interpolation extrapolates. The re-solve must also extend bgrid and re-examine the default region: at 0.1x there are ZERO defaults in 2,163,000 firm-months and z_cut_down is pinned at the grid floor everywhere, so raising sigma_z will make default a live event for the first time, which is desirable (it is the only genuine nonlinearity GS21 has) but changes the equilibrium.

GS21's arbitrary floor P_ex = max(0.05/k, P_ex) at panel_functions_gs21.py line 131 is inert today (minimum realized k*P_ex = 30.4) but is the most plausible source of the 1e9 true SDF weights recorded in the original-vol run: a near-singular cond_var passed to np.linalg.solve, which raises no error. Fix or remove it in the same commit, and add an eigenvalue guard.

KP14 CANNOT BE RECALIBRATED AT ALL until two prior bugs are fixed: integ_results.npz returns exact zeros over the eps interval where 98% of firm-months live (scipy.quad on [0,10] against a CIR transition density with sd ~0.006 -- integ_kp14.py line 43), and G_func.csv was solved under the pre-Jun-18 parameters and is 49x off. kp14_fd.py line 7 does `from parameters_kp14 import *`, a module that does not exist in the repo, so the solfiles cannot currently be regenerated. Fix the quadrature (use a fixed grid over [mean - 8sd, mean + 8sd] of the noncentral chi-square, or scipy's ncx2 moments directly), restore parameters_kp14, and re-solve, before touching sigma_eps.

BGN: widening the sigmaj band changes corr_zj and therefore changes the model's implied cash-flow betas, so the value premium and the calibrated beta_star/scale (fitted to prob_in_money 0.10 and 0.05) should be re-checked.
proposals.implementation_cost: Three one-line parameter edits, but two of them cascade into re-solves: GS21 needs new MATLAB solfiles (external toolchain), KP14 needs kp14_fd.py restored and integ_kp14.py's quadrature rewritten. BGN is genuinely free. No change to the structure or cost of any sdf_compute; the second moment remains analytic in every case.

proposals.name: P5. Metric repair: a scale-free pricing-error statistic, report Sharpe as a fraction of the true maximum, add an unconditional Sharpe, and build test assets with power
proposals.one_line: Replace the leverage-contaminated HJD with sqrt(1 - rho_uncentered^2), propagate the already-computed max_sr into results.pkl so every Sharpe can be read as a fraction of the ceiling, add the unconditional Sharpe so the timing channel is credited, and sort test assets on something the linear span does not already price.
proposals.economic_story: None -- these are correctness fixes to how the experiment is scored, and three of the four are strict repairs rather than choices.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: (a) HJD IS NOT SCALE-FREE AND IS NOT A HANSEN-JAGANNATHAN DISTANCE. It is the RMSE between a method's UNNORMALIZED regression return w'xret and the unit-cost minimum-second-moment portfolio return sdf_ret. Both are projections of the constant 1 onto a return span, so their functional forms match -- E[sdf_ret] = Rf*SR*^2/(1+SR*^2), sd(sdf_ret) = Rf*SR*/(1+SR*^2) -- and HJD^2 = S^2/(1+S^2) - S_f^2/(1+S_f^2) exactly. Two pathologies follow. First, as SR* grows sd(sdf_ret) -> 0 while E[sdf_ret] -> Rf, so HJD for every method converges to ~1.0: at SR* = 2 the entire range between zero skill and perfect correlation is 13.1% of the level and 72% of HJD^2 is the irreducible mean gap; at SR* = 3 it is 8.6% and 83%. Second, driving the ridge alpha up shrinks the method's weights toward zero, giving HJD -> sqrt(E[sdf_ret^2]) mechanically (0.2860 in BGN, 0.2689 in KP14, 0.329 in GS21), and create_slides_tables.find_best_alpha_for_model(..., 'hjd') takes an argmin over the alpha grid -- so the metric can and does select shrinkage-to-nothing over a correctly directed portfolio. GS21's reported FF HJD of 2.3465 alongside the best Fama Sharpe of 0.4433 is a pure over-leverage artifact. The fix: min over c of E[(c*y - z)^2]/E[z^2] = 1 - rho_unc^2 where rho_unc = E[y z]/sqrt(E[y^2]E[z^2]) is the UNCENTERED correlation (uncentered, because both legs are excess returns whose MEAN carries the pricing information). This runs 0 (perfect) to 1 (orthogonal), is comparable across models with different SR*, and removes both pathologies. (b) SHARPE HAS NO DENOMINATOR. The metric is exactly SR_t(w) = SR*_t * cos_{Sigma_t}(w, w*_t) -- an identity, since w'mu/sqrt(w'Sigma w) = [w'Sigma w*/(sqrt(w'Sigma w) sqrt(w*'Sigma w*))]*sqrt(mu'Sigma^{-1}mu). So the reported number is the true maximum Sharpe times a cosine, and without max_sr in the table nobody can tell whether FF at 0.2423 is 10% or 90% of the ceiling -- which is exactly the difference between 'the estimator is failing' and 'the model has nothing to estimate'. max_sr is ALREADY computed in every sdf_loop and stored by calculate_moments.py, but evaluate_sdfs.py never reads it. (c) THE TIMING CHANNEL IS DELETED. mean_t(w'rp_t/sqrt(w'Sigma_t w)) is homogeneous of degree zero in w each month, so a method that correctly levers up when the conditional max Sharpe is high gets exactly zero credit -- and conditional scaling is one of the two channels through which complexity pays in the DKKM/KMZ theory. (d) THE TEST ASSETS HAVE NO POWER: 25 portfolios sorted on mve and bm only, which are two of the five characteristics every method already spans linearly.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Not applicable -- this proposal changes no economics. It is included because without (b) the diagnosis of every other proposal is unfalsifiable, and because (a) is a genuine defect that will be caught in refereeing regardless.
proposals.exact_change: (a) bop-analyze-remote/create_slides_tables.py lines 51-56 (and the parallel block at analyze.py lines 158 and 219): replace `sq_error = (xret - sdf_ret)**2` and its sqrt-of-mean with `rho_unc = (xret*sdf_ret).mean()/sqrt((xret**2).mean()*(sdf_ret**2).mean()); hjd_scaled = sqrt(max(0, 1 - rho_unc**2))`. Keep the old column alongside for one draft. (b) utils/evaluate_sdfs.py line 172, where sdf_ret = m['sdf_ret'] is read: add max_sr = m['max_sr'] and carry it into the all_returns dict at lines 175-179; then in create_slides_tables.py report sharpe/mean(max_sr) as the headline 'Sigma-cosine' column. (c) create_slides_tables.py lines 34-42: alongside the mean-of-ratios, compute the unconditional Sharpe mean_t(mean)/sqrt(mean_t(stdev^2) + var_t(mean)) from the per-month 'mean' and 'stdev' columns already in fama_results/dkkm_results, and also report the MEDIAN of the monthly ratio (the mean is dominated by months where the interpolating solution produces a near-hedged w_t with a tiny denominator). (d) utils/generate_25_portfolios.py lines 112-119: keep the mve x bm 5x5 and ADD two more sets -- 5x5 on (mve, diag(cond_var)) and 10 deciles of the TRUE conditional MVE weight w*_t = solve(cond_var, rp), both available directly from the moments pickle. compute_pricing_errors.py then has assets that load on the part of the truth only a rich basis reaches.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: No free parameters. The scale-free form is derived: least squares through the origin gives min_c E[(c y - z)^2] = E[z^2](1 - (E[yz])^2/(E[y^2]E[z^2])), so dividing by E[z^2] yields exactly 1 - rho_unc^2. The immediate diagnostic the team can run today, before any code change: create_slides_tables.py lines 60-68 already report 'SDF Sharpe' = mean(sdf_ret)/sd(sdf_ret), and by the algebra above that quantity EQUALS SR* exactly. If it exceeds about 1.5 per month, the current HJD is structurally incapable of separating methods at the two decimals printed in the tables, and every HJD number in all_results.pdf should be discarded.
proposals.predicted_effect: Reported HJDs will change substantially and non-uniformly: GS21's FF value of 2.3465 collapses to something in [0,1] and stops being an outlier; the c=1 double-descent HJD explosions (BGN 18.52, GS21 23.57 at P=360, alpha=0) become bounded; the alpha selected by argmin-HJD will move away from the heaviest shrinkage. The new Sigma-cosine column will, on the CURRENT results, show FF at roughly 0.81 of the ceiling in BGN (0.2423/0.2985) and DKKM at 0.85 -- which by itself demonstrates that the estimators are near the ceiling and the DGP is the problem, and is the single most persuasive diagnostic in the paper. The unconditional Sharpe will differ from the conditional one by however much timing matters, which is currently unknown and worth knowing. Sharpe levels and max_sr are unchanged by construction.
risks: A referee will ask why the pricing-error metric changed between drafts. Report both columns and justify the new one from the algebra, not from the results.

Note the asymmetry the current metric has in DKKM's FAVOUR that the fix removes: DKKM gets 6 alphas whose optimum is chosen post hoc on the evaluation metric itself, i.e. six chances at the right leverage, while FF/FM have only alpha = 0 and no way to rescale. A scale-free metric neutralizes this, which will make DKKM look slightly WORSE on pricing error -- disclose that this is the correct direction.

compute_pricing_errors.py's alpha' Sigma^{-1} alpha statistic on 25 portfolios is already the statistically correct object and arguably should carry the argument instead of any HJD variant; consider demoting HJD to a robustness table.

Minor universe mismatch to fix while in the file: evaluate_sdfs.py lines 170-171 subset rp and cond_var to firm_ids (the prepare_panel survivors) but sdf_ret comes from moments over the book>0 universe, so the HJ benchmark and the method returns are not defined over the same assets.
proposals.implementation_cost: Zero cost on sdf_compute. About 20 lines in the analyze repo plus 3 lines in evaluate_sdfs.py plus ~40 lines in generate_25_portfolios.py. No re-run of the simulation is needed for (a), (b) or (c) if the moments pickles are retained -- max_sr is already in them.

proposals.name: P6. Reporting lags with heterogeneous fiscal year-ends, plus HETEROSKEDASTIC (not classical) measurement error in the accounting characteristics
proposals.one_line: Give each firm a fiscal month so accounting chars update once a year and go stale in between, add a 'months since update' observable, and add measurement noise whose VARIANCE depends on firm size -- and do NOT add classical homoskedastic errors-in-variables, because it provably shrinks the DKKM advantage.
proposals.economic_story: Real accounting characteristics are not observed continuously or cleanly. Firms report on staggered fiscal year-ends, the standard convention lags accounting data by 6 months, and reporting quality varies systematically with firm size, age and analyst coverage. In the current panels every characteristic is a noiseless, contemporaneous, invertible function of the latent state -- in GS21 bm = 1/P_ex EXACTLY (verified to machine precision), mkt_lev = b/P_ex, size = log k + log P_ex, and rank-standardized roe is literally the cross-sectional rank of lagged z, so four chars invert the entire 3-dimensional state and an MLP on chars explains 98.3% of the true SDF weight. A correctly specified small model is then the right model by construction.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: The task asks explicitly whether errors-in-variables helps or hurts a nonlinear estimator, and the derivation gives a clean answer with opposite signs for the two cases. CLASSICAL (homoskedastic) EIV HURTS DKKM MORE THAN FM, so it should NOT be added. Proof sketch: if the target is g(x*) and the econometrician sees x = x* + e with e ~ N(0, sigma_e^2 I), the best predictor is the Gaussian convolution E[g(x*)|x] = (g * phi_{sigma_e})(x), whose Fourier transform is ghat(omega) exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2). The LINEAR component (omega -> 0) is attenuated only by the classical factor lambda = tau^2/(tau^2+sigma_e^2), while every nonlinear component is attenuated EXPONENTIALLY in its frequency. Since the RFF basis is exactly a frequency decomposition at frequencies gamma*|w|, the DKKM span advantage decays like exp(-gamma^2 sigma_e^2/2) while FM's decays like lambda. Classical EIV therefore strictly compresses the DKKM-over-FM gap -- realistic, but working against the goal. HETEROSKEDASTIC EIV HELPS. If sigma_e,i^2 = s(z_i) for an observable reliability proxy z_i (firm size, age, months since last report), the optimal predictor becomes lambda_i * g_smoothed(x_i) with lambda_i = tau^2/(tau^2 + s(z_i)) a firm-specific shrinkage factor. The optimal weight therefore contains a MULTIPLICATIVE interaction between the reliability variable and every signal -- a product that is nonlinear in the chars even when g is linear. STALENESS is the same mechanism with a cleaner economic label: if firm i last reported h_i months ago, the accounting char's informativeness decays in h_i, so the efficient weight is lambda(h_i) * bm_i, and because fiscal year-ends are staggered, h_i varies cross-sectionally within every month, which makes this a live cross-sectional interaction rather than a date-level effect.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: FM applies ONE coefficient per characteristic to every firm in the cross-section, so it cannot apply a firm-specific attenuation lambda_i to a signal; the best it can do is add h_i as a separate additive regressor, which is not the same object -- the truth is lambda(h_i)*bm_i, a product, not lambda*h_i + b*bm_i. FF is the interesting partial exception and must be conceded: FF's 2x3 design contains exactly one interaction, size x char, so if reliability depended on size alone FF would get a two-bin approximation of the attenuation. That is why the reliability proxy should be STALENESS (months since last report), which is orthogonal to size by construction under staggered fiscal year-ends and is NOT one of FF's sort variables -- and why one would have to add a third sort dimension (2 x 3 x 3 = 18 portfolios per characteristic) to give FF a chance, which is exactly the dimensionality blow-up that motivates a flexible estimator. A Fourier basis represents lambda(h)*bm(x) as a smooth bivariate function at no extra cost.
proposals.exact_change: MEASUREMENT ONLY -- nothing in any sdf_compute and no re-solve. NEW helper in utils_factors/char_library.py (the same file as P3): (1) assign each firm a fixed fiscal month fm_i ~ Uniform{0..11} at generation; (2) after each model's create_panel, for every ACCOUNTING characteristic (book, op_cash_flow, and everything derived from them -- bm, roe, agr, book_lev), replace the contemporaneous value with the value from the firm's most recent fiscal month, lagged an additional 6 months (utils_bgn/panel_functions_bgn.py lines 240-260 is where these are built; the KP14 and GS21 equivalents are the corresponding blocks in their create_panel); market-based chars (mve, size, mom) stay contemporaneous, which is the standard convention and creates a real timing wedge between the two families; (3) add the observable char stale_i,t = months since the firm's last fiscal update, in 0..11; (4) add multiplicative noise to the accounting chars only: bm_obs = bm * exp(sigma_e,i * u), u ~ iid N(0,1), with sigma_e,i = sigma_e0 * (mve_i/median)^{-xi}. Wire the new columns into config.py CHARS lists and CHAR_TO_FACTOR.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: STALENESS: 12-month fiscal cycle plus the conventional 6-month reporting lag means the accounting information age h_i,t runs 6 to 17 months with a uniform cross-sectional distribution -- no free parameter, this is the Fama-French convention. Its bite is set by how fast the underlying state moves: in BGN book = I*num changes only when a project is created or dies, so a 12-month stale bm is nearly as good as a fresh one and the effect will be small; in GS21 z has monthly persistence rho_z = 0.9655, so a 12-month lag attenuates the roe signal by rho_z^12 = 0.657 and the cross-sectional variation in h (6 to 17 months) generates attenuation factors from rho^6 = 0.810 to rho^17 = 0.552, a 1.47x spread -- enough for the interaction to matter. HETEROSKEDASTIC NOISE: calibrate the reliability spread to the accounting-quality literature via the ratio of signal-to-total variance, targeting lambda = 0.90 at the 90th size percentile and lambda = 0.50 at the 10th. lambda = tau^2/(tau^2+sigma_e^2) gives sigma_e/tau = sqrt((1-lambda)/lambda) = 0.333 at the top and 1.000 at the bottom, i.e. a 3.0x spread in noise sd across the size distribution. With sd(log mve) = S in a given model, xi = log(3.0)/(2.563*S) and sigma_e0 = the geometric mean 0.577*tau. In BGN with S ~ 0.6, xi = 1.099/1.538 = 0.71. DO NOT add a homoskedastic component: by the Fourier argument above, a common sigma_e attenuates the DKKM-reachable nonlinear content by exp(-gamma^2 sigma_e^2/2), which at the P2-rescaled gamma of 5.1 and sigma_e/tau = 0.58 in rank units (tau^2 = 1/12) is exp(-5.1^2*0.58^2/12/2) = exp(-0.36) = 0.70 -- a 30% haircut on exactly the components the proposal exists to create. State this trade-off explicitly in the paper; it is a genuine and interesting theoretical point in its own right.
proposals.predicted_effect: Small on its own -- expect the DKKM/FM Sharpe ratio to move by perhaps 5-15%, and possibly DOWN in BGN where the accounting state is nearly static so staleness costs information without creating a usable interaction. Its main value is as an inexpensive realism layer that (i) breaks the GS21 identity bm = 1/P_ex exactly, which is currently the single most indefensible feature of that panel, (ii) supplies a reliability variable that turns every other characteristic's coefficient into a firm-specific function, multiplying the effect of P1 and P3, and (iii) lets the paper make a real theoretical contribution about when errors-in-variables helps versus hurts high-dimensional estimators. max_sr is unchanged (this is measurement, not DGP), and FF/FM Sharpes fall slightly from the attenuation, so the gap widens partly by lowering the benchmark -- which must be disclosed.
risks: The gap can widen partly because FF/FM get WORSE rather than because DKKM gets better. Report the population span ceiling (SR_rff/SR_lin computed on the true moments with the observed chars) so the two are distinguishable.

In BGN the accounting state (book = I*num, a small integer averaging 5.95) barely moves month to month, so staleness may be nearly free and the whole mechanism inert there. Check sd(bm_stale - bm_fresh)/sd(bm) before committing.

Adding multiplicative noise to bm and roe worsens the existing tie/degeneracy problems (agr is 91% zeros in BGN and 98.8% zeros in GS21) in one direction -- it breaks the ties, which is good -- but it also makes the FF tercile sorts on those chars pure noise sorts, which will look like sabotage of FF unless the tie problem is fixed properly at fama_functions.py lines 86-88 in the same commit.

The heteroskedastic-noise story requires the reliability proxy to be observable. Using months-since-report is clean; using size is not, because FF's 2x3 design already contains size interactions and the referee will say FF was given a fair chance and used it.
proposals.implementation_cost: Zero on sdf_compute -- the true conditional moments are computed from the model's latent states and are entirely unaffected by what the econometrician is shown. No re-solve of kp14_fd.py and no new GS21 solfiles. About 60 lines in char_library.py plus config edits. One caveat: the fiscal-month assignment must be generated with the panel (it needs a per-firm draw stored alongside firmid), so panels must be regenerated -- but the expensive step, calculate_moments, does NOT need to be re-run if the underlying model parameters are unchanged.
